tables.title: System inventory
tables.description: Every system, tool, portal and shared spreadsheet used to run the business. Include named spreadsheets, not just software. The column that matters most is "Data held nowhere else" - that is what has to be migrated or replaced. Include your A/P platform, A/R or collections tool, TMS or freight system, ecommerce platform, marketplace seller accounts, EDI provider, 3PL and warehouse portals, payroll, expense and card systems, forecasting models, and quality or specification systems.
columns: Could we turn it off afterward?

example.Data held nowhere else: Freight cost per shipment before invoice arrives
example.Could we turn it off afterward?: Probably - if freight cost lands in the ERP

tables.title: System of record
tables.description: For each type of data, the one place considered authoritative today. Where two systems disagree, tell us which wins and who decides.

example.Authoritative system today: 3PL portal, reconciled weekly to a spreadsheet
example.Notes: Portal and spreadsheet drift between reconciliations

presetDataTypes: Item / SKU list (and who can create one)
Pricing by customer, channel, volume tier

tables.title: Critical spreadsheets
tables.description: The ten spreadsheets the business could least afford to lose. The key column is "Logic that exists nowhere else" - allocation rules, cost buildups, accrual estimates, tiered pricing, commission splits, yield assumptions.
columns: Report, or a system holding data?

tables.title: Interfaces
tables.description: Every place data moves between two systems. Include manual ones - a person exporting a CSV and importing it elsewhere is an interface. The last two columns are SYS-6: who owns it and what it is built on.

reports.title: Recurring reports
reports.description: Everything produced on a schedule, including anything assembled by hand in Excel. Add rows as needed. Delete the grey example row once you start.

example.Problem if it disappeared?: Yes - CEO runs the week off it
